A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 46-page versions of the same adaptive Bregman Frank–Wolfe study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite the changed title and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 Section 6 reports original optimization experiments, including convergence plots and numerical comparisons across 20 problem instances.

after.justification: V2 Section 6 and Appendix E report original experiments, including retained studies, new gas-sensor evaluations, and larger phase-retrieval problems.

M1.justification: The FW directions and Bregman step formula remain, but Algorithm 2's printed control flow changes: v1 returns when the descent bound holds; v2 continues while it holds and tests x+ before assigning it. Algorithm 3 moves its explicit exponent search into optional prose. These are localized procedural revisions, without evidence that the experimental implementation changed.

E1.justification: V2 adds real gas-sensor data to the existing ℓp loss task. All five earlier problem families, including synthetic and MovieLens NMF, remain represented. Larger phase-retrieval dimensions change experimental settings rather than task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding retained experiments preserve their comparator sets, including mirror descent for nonnegative inverse problems and EucAFW, ShortAFW, and OpenAFW for away-step phase retrieval. The new gas-sensor comparison uses existing EucFW and OpenFW baselines; no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: Ordinary phase retrieval changes from (m,n)=(100,2000), K=200 to (1000,10000) and (2000,10000), K=2000. OpenFW's budget increases from 1000 to 5000 iterations while other methods retain 1000. New gas-sensor experiments specify 13910 observations, 128 variables, radii 130 and 200, and all-ones initialization. These substantially revise the evaluated scales and budget allocation.

E4.justification: Neither version provides dedicated component ablations, distribution-shift tests, or error analyses. V2's additional constraint radii and phase-retrieval sizes are presented as benchmark settings, without a separate sensitivity or mechanism analysis.

E5.justification: V1's empirical tables report means only; v2 Tables 2–8 report means and standard deviations across 20 instances. V2 also discloses seeds 1234 and 42 for synthetic experiments. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in the previously reported instance counts.

E6.justification: V2 adds gas-sensor results and replaces v1's ordinary phase-retrieval results with two larger configurations, reporting BregFW mean primal gaps of 1.3107e-11 and 6.6743e-12 in Tables 4–5. These are different-setting results. Retained Table 3 also changes beyond rounding: BregFW's FW gap changes from 0.3764084 to 0.37686. Most other retained table means are merely rounded.

T1.justification: Most proofs, including v1's uniformly convex-set appendix results, are retained and relocated. V2 changes the standing scaling-exponent range from 0<ν≤1 to ν>0 in Lemma A.3 and several convergence statements. The convex away-step polynomial-bound coefficient also changes non-equivalently in Theorems 4.4/C.4 versus v1 Theorem 4.6, while the underlying proof remains essentially unchanged.

C1.justification: The principal algorithm, convergence, and empirical-performance claims remain. V2's introduction adds an explicit priority claim: the first FW algorithm with linear-convergence guarantees for a restricted nonconvex problem class, with novelty also claimed for the L-smooth setting. V1 presented these results without that explicit priority claim.

C2.justification: V2 Section 7 adds substantive interpretation and future directions: it argues that matching objective and kernel structure makes q=1+ν natural, discusses the difficulty of relaxing quadratic growth, and proposes exploring DC optimization. The underlying linear-versus-sublinear rate cases already appeared in v1.

D1.justification: V2 adds gas-sensor dataset access information and documents a global FW-gap stopping threshold of 10^-7. V1 stated iteration limits without this threshold, so its addition establishes new disclosure rather than a confirmed change to earlier runs. Software, hardware, and line-search hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Yang and Toh's inexact Bregman proximal-gradient work and removes several references, including the self-concordant FW studies by Carderera et al. and Dvurechensky et al. It shortens the detailed comparison with Vyguzov and Stonyakin and makes the nonconvex linear-convergence novelty claim more explicit.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten around a research question and contribution bullets. Preliminaries and convergence sections are condensed, most proofs move into Appendices A–D, experiments are divided between Section 6 and Appendix E, and a conclusion with limitations and future work is added. The title and acceleration terminology also change.

P2.justification: V2 introduces four compact main-text figures for gas-sensor and larger phase-retrieval experiments, removes the earlier ordinary phase-retrieval display, and relocates retained experimental figures and tables to Appendix E. NMF figures become side-by-side displays, and empirical tables expand to accommodate standard deviations. These changes substantially reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: New gas-sensor evidence, larger experiments, standard deviations, and clearer organization improve coverage and transparency. However, v2 Algorithm 2 introduces an uninitialized-variable test and reverses the role of the acceptance condition, while Theorem 4.4 changes a bound coefficient inconsistently with its retained proof. These central specification problems counteract the gains; the PDFs do not resolve whether the problematic pseudocode reflects the implementation used, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
